# Activate the contribution and release gates

Workflow files define checks; repository settings make those checks mandatory. The private repository's current plan refused rulesets and branch protection on October 11, 2026 (`403: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public`). These templates are ready to apply after upgrading or the separately authorized public launch. Nothing in this document changes repository visibility.

An audit-only rerun on existing main started on a GitHub runner and passed at 20:46 UTC on October 11, 2026, after the owner's billing update. Direct job metadata confirms that successful fifth attempt; the overall run still shows failure, with no execution steps for its other jobs. This establishes runner availability at that time, not current billing status or validation of the proposed combined source and complete hosted matrix. Earlier attempts were refused before execution because of billing/spending limits. Check the individual jobs and attempt when reviewing the run. The private-plan restriction on required rules remains separate and was still present after the successful probe.

The repository's action SHA-pinning policy and selected-action allowlist were enabled and verified on October 11, 2026. The allowlist covers the 14 action paths used by local and remote workflows, including their pinned composite-action dependencies, across 11 external repositories. Blanket allowances for GitHub-owned and Marketplace-verified actions are disabled. Actions remains enabled; workflow tokens still default to read-only, with Actions creating/approving PRs disabled. The remaining branch/release protections below are still setup requirements.

The approved repositories are `actions/attest`, `actions/attest-build-provenance`, `actions/checkout`, `actions/dependency-review-action`, `actions/download-artifact`, `actions/setup-go`, `actions/setup-node`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `github/codeql-action`, `ossf/scorecard-action`, and `zizmorcore/zizmor-action`. The configured patterns name the used action paths with `@*`; the separate SHA-pinning policy still requires a full commit SHA. When adding or updating an action, inspect its composite dependencies and update the explicit path allowlist before merging if it introduces a new path. Local reusable workflows remain allowed. [GitHub documents these controls](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-github-actions-settings-for-a-repository#allowing-select-actions-and-reusable-workflows-to-run).

## Contribution settings

1. Allow only approved GitHub Actions and require actions to use full commit SHAs. Use read-only default workflow permissions; turn off Actions creating/approving pull requests. Do not grant write tokens or secrets to fork workflows. Require approval for workflows from outside collaborators. Use GitHub-hosted disposable runners for public contributions, never a maintainer's computer or a privileged persistent runner.
2. Wait for the first successful run on the exact proposed source. Required status names are **CI required** and **Security required**, both produced by the **GitHub Actions** app (ID 15368). The gate jobs run on every PR and merge-group, without path filters, and reject failed, skipped, missing or cancelled prerequisites. CodeQL and dependency review explicitly remain unavailable on the current private plan; a public repository requires both when applicable.
3. Apply [rulesets/main.json](rulesets/main.json) through Settings → Rules → Rulesets → Import, or the API below. The owner chose solo maintenance: every change still requires a pull request, resolved review threads, and both status checks from the GitHub Actions app, but no second-person approval is required. CODEOWNERS routes review requests without making a solo maintainer's own changes impossible to merge. The ruleset also requires **CodeQL results**, blocking security alerts at **Medium or higher** and other alerts at **Errors**. A successful analysis job only proves the scan ran; this separate `code_scanning` rule enforces its findings. It denies deletion and force push. No bypass is configured. A maintainer must review contribution diffs before merging, especially edits to the checks themselves.
4. Protect release tags with [rulesets/release-tags.json](rulesets/release-tags.json). Tag creation remains restricted by repository write access; existing `v*` tags cannot be changed or deleted. Keep write access small. Consider a separate creation ruleset with an explicitly selected release team if more contributors gain write access.
5. Enable Dependabot security updates, secret scanning with push protection and private vulnerability reporting. Review workflow, permission-boundary and release-tool changes carefully: checks alone cannot stop a contributor from proposing weaker checks. CODEOWNERS covers the entire repository for review routing; under the solo-maintainer policy its approval is advisory. Keep repository write access limited to trusted maintainers. When another trusted maintainer is available, independently required review can be enabled as a separate policy change.

With repository administration authorization, run once per template (replace OWNER/REPO with the actual public repository):

```sh
gh api --method POST repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/main.json
gh api --method POST repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --input .github/rulesets/release-tags.json
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets
```

Do not repeat POST blindly; update the returned rule ID for later revisions. Before activating the code scanning rule, obtain successful CodeQL analyses on `main` and the proposed PR; GitHub requires results for both refs. Confirm the active remote ruleset contains the CodeQL tool and the thresholds above. On the current private plan these scans and protections remain unavailable; keep the public contribution gate pending rather than removing the rule to make checks green.

Do not turn on automatic merging until a deliberate failing PR and a subsequent passing PR prove the remote protections work. Include a disposable PR that produces a CodeQL security alert at the configured threshold: after analysis completes, GitHub must still block merging; remove the fixture and verify it clears. Local policy tests validate the template, not GitHub enforcement. Code scanning merge protection applies to qualifying alerts in a PR's changed lines; it is not a promise that the whole repository has no vulnerabilities. GitHub also excludes merge queue groups from this protection. Both execution workflows handle `merge_group`, but keep strict up-to-date PR checks and leave merge queue disabled until alert blocking is separately qualified for the chosen queue policy. See [GitHub's merge protection limits](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/merge-protection).

## Protected npm publishing

1. Create a GitHub environment named **npm-release** with the owner as a required reviewer and **Prevent self-review** disabled for solo maintenance. Each release still waits for an explicit manual environment approval; a successful tag build cannot publish on its own. Add a custom deployment rule of type **Tag**, pattern **v***, and no branch rules. Turn off administrator bypass. The release workflow checks that a required reviewer exists, administrator bypass is disabled, and only the release-tag pattern is allowed before building. A later team can enable Prevent self-review without changing the workflow.
2. Configure the npm package's trusted publisher for the public GitHub owner/repository, workflow **release.yml**, environment **npm-release**, allowing publish. This replaces the long-lived `NPM_TOKEN`; no repository npm token is used by the workflow. Confirm the publisher details match after a repository rename. Do not weaken the workflow to fall back to a token when configuration fails.
3. Confirm `package.json.repository.url` matches the public repository. A release tag must identify a commit already on `main`, match the package version, and have dated changelog notes. The same full CI and security checks run again on the tag.
4. Review the immutable `verified-release-candidate` artifact and its test reports, then approve the environment deployment. Both npm and portable archives must pass installation tests and remain byte-for-byte identical to their verification receipt; handoff copies the archives without repacking. A fresh publishing runner downloads only that same-run artifact, verifies checksums, attests it and publishes with `--ignore-scripts --provenance`. It does not check out source, install dependencies or rebuild anything with publishing authority.
5. Verify npm provenance and downloaded archives after release. GitHub attestations prove provenance, not that an application is harmless. Keep physical-device and real-provider qualification evidence alongside the release record.

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
gh attestation verify nalebc-reach-VERSION.tgz --repo OWNER/REPO
```

Protected environments and repository rules depend on the GitHub plan. The release workflow deliberately fails closed while the repository is private or the review environment is missing; successful local tests do not activate those settings.

References: [GitHub Actions secure use](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use), [code scanning merge protection setup](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/manage-your-configuration/set-merge-protection), [ruleset API and supported thresholds](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules#create-a-repository-ruleset), [merge queues](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue), [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).
